rv.q: This West End transfer is a success – the Ambassadors' petite stage perfectly conjures a black and white television screen blown up to theatrical proportions.

Each element – from Jones’ direction to Paul Steinberg’s set and Sarah Angliss and Christopher Shutt’s sound design – is incredibly well done and, even if the show doesn’t always hang together as a whole, it’s still enjoyable and entertaining.
Yet for all that skill, The Twilight Zone play comes to feel like a bad idea, well executed.
Spooky TV tribute could do with an extra dimension.
The result is a show that feels oddly cheaper than the original – and weirdly unexciting.
The tone, lying in the middle ground between thriller and comedy, is struck perfectly by the excellent ensemble cast, all playing a variety of roles.
The humour alone is a sufficient sweetener to make this extra-terrestrial entertainment a theatrical treat...
As a production however, I think this show is faultless; it's the story that makes it difficult to really feel wowed by it.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this theatrical adaptation of the cult TV series, with some praising Washburn's weird, theatrically inventive approach while others find the retro anthology format an odd fit for the West End stage.
